title: Tanzanian Calamari
community: Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania — the most popular seafood starter
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Calamari — fresh calamari rings in a spiced flour and semolina batter, deep-fried until golden and crispy in 2—3 minutes. Served with pili pili mayo and lemon. The most popular seafood starter at Tanzanian coastal restaurants.
longDesc: Fresh calamari from the Indian Ocean, battered and fried in 3 minutes. The semolina in the batter gives a far crunchier coating than plain flour alone.
ingredients: 500g fresh calamari — cleaned and sliced into rings
Pili pili mayo (4 tbsp mayo + 1 tbsp pili pili sauce)
steps: Mix flour, semolina, and all spices.
Toss calamari in seasoned flour. Shake off excess.
Fry in small batches 2—3 minutes until golden.
Serve immediately with pili pili mayo and lemon.
cookingScience: Semolina has larger particles than flour — creating more air pockets in the coating, producing a lighter, crunchier crust that stays crispy longer.
sustainabilityTips: Fresh Indian Ocean calamari from local fishermen.
culturalNote: Calamari at a Zanzibar beach restaurant — cold drink in hand, the Indian Ocean in front — is one of the finest simple pleasures the island offers.
